stages.report:
FALSIFIED
The belief that after a 10% drop in one day XRP recovers over the next 3 days is falsified on past data because it did not beat its pre-registered benchmark.

**What was tested**
Rule: When XRP/USDT closes down more than 10% in a day, buy at the next day's open and sell at the close 3 days later. Window 2018-05-04 to 2026-10-29. n_signals 60, n_trades 52, avg_bars_held 3.0, exposure_pct 5.03. Backtest: mean_net_pct 2.14, median_net_pct 3.15, total_net_pct 110.79, max_drawdown_pct -37.31, buy_and_hold_total_pct 39.08, win_rate_pct 59.62, t_stat 1.27.

**Strongest evidence against**
Random-entry baseline. Rule mean 2.14% vs random-entry mean 0.22%. The rule beat 92% of 2000 random sets, one-sided p = 0.079. Pre-registered criterion requires mean_net_return beats random_entries at alpha 0.05 with min_trades 20. p = 0.079 > 0.050, so primary test fails.

**What held up**
Sample size pass: 52 completed trades from 60 signals. Look-ahead guard pass: conditions use only past and current bars; every trade opens at next bar's open. Indicators used: ret(1). Multiple testing pass: first sealed belief about XRP/USDT; no correction needed. Fees pass: at 0.25% per side mean trade is 1.84%; edge disappears at about 117 bps per side. Time split pass: positive in both halves: 2.11% (n=38) then 2.23% (n=14). Neighbourhood pass: 6 of 6 nearby variants point same way (median 1.93%). Cross asset pass: beats random entries on 9 of 9 other assets (6 significant at 5%).

**What would change the verdict**
A one-sided p-value < 0.050 for beating random entries under the pre-registered criterion, or a re-registered test with a different benchmark.

**Caveats**
Falsify tests beliefs about the past. It is not investment advice and makes no prediction.
